rounds.text: Nupur Recyclers Ltd is demonstrating exceptional operational momentum, highlighted by a compounded sales growth of 41% over the trailing twelve months and a quarterly operating margin expanding to 12% in June 2026 compared to 8% in the year-ago period [E15, E23]. Profitability is compounding at 27% over the trailing twelve months alongside a robust rules-based screen score of 82 out of 100 driven by strong sales and net profit growth [E17, E57, E58, E60]. The business is backed by high-quality fundamentals, including an ROCE of 15.1% and a healthy cash conversion of 1.12x for March 2026 where profits are fully backed by operating cash flows [E12, E26]. Furthermore, institutional confidence is building, with foreign institutions increasing their holding to 1.29% as of September 2026 and promoters raising their stake to 73.60%, generating positive money flow [E33, E34, E36]. The market's appreciation of these dynamics is reflected in a 141.1% twelve-month price return, a relative-strength rating of 100 against the Nifty 500, and a technical posture where the price remains above both its 50-day and 200-day moving averages [E42, E43, E44]. Conceded: the stock trades at an elevated P/E of 63.2x, a price-to-book ratio of 8.09x, and a negative DCF margin of safety [E1, E2, E38].

The current market valuation of Nupur Recyclers Ltd is detached from intrinsic reality, trading at an alarming P/E of 63.2x and a price-to-book multiple of 8.09x against filed statements [E1, E2]. These multiples vastly outstrip sector benchmarks, where the sector P/E sits at 14.76x and EV/EBITDA stands at 9.62x, pointing to extreme overvaluation [E6, E11]. A rigorous discounted cash flow model values the stock at a mere Rs 46 per share compared to its market price of Rs 157, resulting in a staggering negative margin of safety of -243.4% [E37, E38]. Furthermore, the reverse DCF indicates that today’s price demands an aggressive 22.0% earnings growth rate, which dwarfs the modest 5.0% growth assumed in the base case [E39]. Compounded sales and profit growth over a three-year period have both stalled at a pedestrian 5%, exposing a glaring disconnect between historical operational velocity and the lofty expectations currently priced into the stock [E14, E16]. Operational quality also bears scrutiny, as earnings are padded by Rs 12.3 Cr in other income, debtor days have lengthened from 30.9 to 38.4 days, and the yearly operating-margin trend is flagged as inconsistent [E24, E55, E56]. Conceded: the company displays strong trailing twelve-month momentum with a 41% surge in sales, a 27% increase in profit, and a conservative debt-to-equity ratio of 0.25x [E15, E17, E29].

Conceded: the P/E of 63.2x and P/B of 8.09x look demanding on backward-looking metrics [E1, E2], but static multiples miss a dramatic inflecting acceleration in the underlying business. The bear leans heavily on a static DCF of Rs 46 [E37], but ignores that forward catalysts are already materialising through a +100% surge in capital work-in-progress (CWIP) to Rs 6 Cr for future capacity expansion [E32]. Conceded: the three-year sales and profit growth rates sat at 5% [E14, E16], but trailing twelve-month figures show a massive breakout with sales up 41% and profits up 27% [E15, E17], backed by a rules-based screen score of 82/100 featuring net profit growth of 82% YoY [E60]. Operational efficiency is superior to the broader sector, boasting an ROA of 10.01% against a 5.25% benchmark [E8] and an ROCE of 14.2% versus 10.39% [E10]. Furthermore, institutional confidence is building rather than fleeing, evidenced by foreign institutions increasing their stake and positive money flow signatures [E34, E36], while profits are fully backed by robust cash conversion of 1.12x [E26].

Conceded: trailing twelve-month sales are up 41% and profits are up 27% [E15, E17], and ROCE outperforms the sector at 14.2% [E10]. However, the bull's dismissal of the DCF of Rs 46 ignores a gaping -243.4% margin of safety [E37, E38]. Conceded: CWIP has surged +100% to Rs 6 Cr [E32], but this nascent expansion sits alongside rising borrowings, which jumped from Rs 13 Cr to Rs 33 Cr [E31]. The bull relies heavily on growth metrics, but price growth has outpaced profit growth by 105% while yearly operating margins remain inconsistent [E24, E49]. Furthermore, reported earnings are padded by Rs 12.3 Cr of other income [E55], and debtor days have stretched from 30.9 to 38.4 days [E56]. Finally, institutional interest remains negligible overall, with domestic institutions actually trimming their stake to 0.06% [E35], while the stock trades at an exorbitant P/E of 63.2 against a sector benchmark of just 14.76x [E1, E6].

Conceded: the DCF intrinsic value sits at Rs 46 [E37]. However, treating static DCF models as gospel ignores that the company is in an active expansion phase with CWIP surging 100% to Rs 6 Cr and TTM sales exploding by 41% [E15, E32]. Conceded: borrowings rose to Rs 33 Cr [E31], but this is backed by conservative financing reflected in a healthy debt-to-equity ratio of 0.25x and robust short-term liquidity with a current ratio of 5.28x [E29, E30]. Conceded: debtor days increased to 38.4 days [E56] and earnings include Rs 12.3 Cr of other income [E55], yet profits are fully backed by cash with a 1.12x cash conversion rate, generating Rs 18 Cr in operating cash flow [E26, E27]. Conceded: domestic institutions trimmed their stake slightly [E35], but overall institutional money flow is positive with foreign institutions expanding their holdings and total promoter commitment rising to 73.60% [E33, E34, E36]. Finally, the premium valuation and strong price performance—including a relative-strength rating of 100 and a 141.1% twelve-month return—are justified by operational outperformance, featuring an ROCE of 14.2% outperforming the sector benchmark of 10.39% alongside expanding operating margins [E10, E22, E23, E43, E44].

Conceded: CWIP surged 100% to Rs 6 Cr and TTM sales grew 41% [E15, E32]. However, the bull's dismissal of the DCF intrinsic value of Rs 46 ignores that today's price of Rs 157 already prices in an aggressive 22.0% earnings growth against a historical base case of just 5.0% [E1, E37, E39]. Conceded: debt-to-equity is 0.25x and the current ratio is 5.28x [E29, E30], but borrowings more than doubled to Rs 33 Cr in Mar 2026 from Rs 13 Cr a year earlier alongside rising debtor days of 38.4 [E31, E56]. Conceded: operating cash flow reached Rs 18 Cr with 1.12x cash conversion [E26, E27], yet reported earnings lean heavily on a notable Rs 12.3 Cr of other income [E55]. Conceded: promoters hold 73.60% and FIIs increased stakes [E33, E34], but domestic institutions have trimmed their exposure [E35]. Finally, while the bull points to strong relative strength and a 141.1% twelve-month return [E43, E44], this price-led momentum has pushed the P/E to a lofty 63.2x and price-to-book to 8.09x—vastly outstripping sector benchmarks and leaving a severe margin of safety of -243.4% [E1, E2, E6, E7, E38].
